instructions:
Below is an essay you revised once. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 420 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Essay:

Dear Principal,

I am writing about if every student should have to do community service. I think our school should make it required, but it should be flexible because students are already really busy.

Some of my friends already volunteer and I have seen what it does for them. My friend Maya helps second graders with reading every Tuesday after school. At first she said she only did it because her mom made her. Now she talks about her kids all the time and she gets really excited when one of them finishes a chapter book. She is more patient now and she is not as scared to talk in front of people. Another friend, Daniel, joined a group on the weekends that cleans up trash in the creek behind the shopping center. He told me he never knew how much trash was in our town until he spent a whole morning pulling bottles and plastic bags out of the water. Now he picks up trash even when nobody is looking. Stuff like this teaches you responsibility in a way that sitting in class can't.

I also get why some students don't like the idea. A lot of us have jobs, sports practice, music lessons, or little brothers and sisters to babysit. Homework already takes forever every night. If the school made us do fifty hours a semester, some kids would fall behind or not get enough sleep, and it would feel like a punishment instead of a way to help. That would kind of ruin the whole point.

That's why I think the rule should be reasonable. Maybe twenty hours a year would be enough, and students could pick when and how they do them. If someone works on weekdays they could help at a food bank on Saturday. Someone who plays a sport could coach a little kids team in the off season. The school could even count things kids already do, like helping out at a church event or reading to people at the hospital. If students get to choose, the hours would actually mean something and not feel forced.

Making it required would also help kids who would never volunteer on their own just because they don't know how to start. A lot of people only find out they like helping after they try it.

Our community gives us a lot, like parks, libraries, and teachers. A small, flexible requirement would teach students to give back. I hope you think about it.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
